content: 1. Seven strategies have been identified to help countries and communities prioritize effective programs aimed at preventing violence against children. These strategies are designed to focus on the most promising interventions to protect children from harm. 2. The Global Disability Action Plan 2014–2021 supports the implementation of measures that uphold the rights of persons with disabilities as outlined in the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. It includes actions to ensure access to healthcare services, including rehabilitation, habilitation, and assistive devices, improve disability data collection and monitoring, and promote awareness and understanding of disability. 3. A document outlines ten strategies to enhance road safety for children. These include controlling speed, reducing drinking and driving, promoting helmet use for cyclists and motorcyclists, restraining children in vehicles, improving children’s visibility, enhancing road infrastructure, adapting vehicle design, reducing risks for young drivers, providing appropriate care for injured children, and supervising children near roads. 4. Maternal mental health has a direct impact on childcare practices and nurturing care. The mhGAP intervention guide provides psychosocial interventions for maternal mental health, integrating the management of priority mental health conditions through clinical decision-making algorithms for use by healthcare professionals and planners. 5. A World Health Assembly resolution emphasizes the need for countries to address the specific needs of individuals with autism spectrum disorders and other developmental disorders. This should be integrated into policies and programs related to early childhood and adolescent development as part of a comprehensive approach to mental health and developmental disorders. 6. A WHO toolkit has been developed to enhance preparedness for Zika virus outbreaks. It provides guidance for public health planners and healthcare professionals on necessary infrastructure, resources, and technical measures to manage complications associated with the Zika virus. 7. The Thinking Healthy manual outlines evidence-based psychosocial interventions for addressing perinatal depression. It highlights the role of community health workers in implementing these interventions, with research from countries like Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, and Peru demonstrating their feasibility, effectiveness, and cultural acceptability. 8. A secure and safe environment is critical for nurturing care. The Atlas on Children’s Health and the Environment reviews major environmental hazards to children’s health, including those arising from urbanization, industrialization, globalization, and climate change. It also highlights the role of the health sector in reducing environmental exposures. 9. A report on water and sanitation presents data from 94 countries, emphasizing the importance of increasing access and reducing inequalities in sanitation and drinking water. It also includes data from external support agencies representing over 90% of official development assistance in this area. 10. A report on air pollution and child health summarizes scientific evidence on the adverse health effects of air pollution on children. It aims to motivate healthcare professionals to take action to prevent harm to children’s health caused by air pollution exposure. 11. Neonatal care is essential for optimal child development. Recommendations include engaging caregivers in newborn care, promoting skin-to-skin contact, breastfeeding, and sensory stimulation. This approach strengthens caregiver-infant bonding and facilitates the transition to home care. 12. Guidance is provided for managing serious bacterial infections in young infants in resource-limited settings where referral care is not feasible. Community health workers play a key role in identifying signs of serious infections and providing outpatient care. 13. The Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) includes treatment algorithms for common childhood conditions such as respiratory infections, diarrhea, fever, malnutrition, and HIV. Training modules are available for both in-person and distance learning. 14. Home-based maternal, newborn, and child health records improve care-seeking behaviors, male involvement, maternal and child home care practices, and communication between healthcare providers and families. 15. Standards for improving the quality of care for children and adolescents in health facilities emphasize addressing their unique physical, psychosocial, developmental, and communication needs. The framework includes eight domains for improving care quality and addressing common conditions affecting children and adolescents. 16. Guidelines on physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep for young children provide recommendations to promote early childhood development and prevent obesity. These guidelines are part of the Ending Childhood Obesity initiative. 17. A report from the Commission on Ending Childhood Obesity outlines recommended actions for policymakers to halt the rise in childhood obesity. It recognizes the varying prevalence and contributing factors across countries and provides tailored recommendations for intervention. 18. Caregiving interventions that promote early learning in the first three years of life have been shown to improve cognitive, motor, and socioemotional development in children. Integrated caregiving and nutrition interventions further enhance child growth and development outcomes. 19. Supporting maternal mental health is a key influence on early childhood development outcomes. Psychological interventions for depression and anxiety in pregnant women and new mothers improve cognitive, language, and motor development in children while addressing maternal mental health challenges.
